## VERDICT PAYLOADS

MERGE C0020 <- F001  
Evidence: My independently derived duplicate-`finding_id` finding has the same root cause as C0020/C0007: `build_feedback_records()` builds `finding_by_id` with a last-wins dict comprehension, so duplicate IDs silently collapse and feedback can be misrouted. This is already settled in the registry. No new discovery filed.

MERGE C0005 <- F002  
Evidence: My independently derived final-verdict coverage finding has the same root cause as C0005: `build_feedback_records()` iterates only `cell_verdicts.items()`, so `final_verdicts={"F1": "REJECTED"}` with `cell_verdicts={}` emits no feedback. This is already settled in the registry. No new discovery filed.

MERGE C0017 <- F003  
Evidence: My independently derived near-duplicate ordering finding has the same root cause as C0017/C0019: duplicate feedback is only attached to `fid_a`, so a pair emitted as `(prior_id, current_id, sim)` is dropped when only the current finding is present. This is already settled in the registry. No new discovery filed.

## DISCOVERY FINDINGS

No new admissible CRITICAL/HIGH findings filed in this round.

## GLOBAL P-PASS

Pass 1: Compared my three independently found issues against the Round 8 registry.  
Result: all three are already present as settled or confirmed canonical findings: duplicate ID collapse, final-only rejected verdict loss, and near-duplicate order dependence.

Pass 2: Checked whether any of my findings add a distinct mechanism, broader consequence, or new edge case beyond the canonical entries.  
Result: no. The mechanisms and downstream consequences are already represented.

Pass 3: Checked for contradictions between the three fixes I previously proposed.  
Result: no direct contradiction. The duplicate-ID fail-closed fix is foundational; if applied, it prevents misrouting across the other feedback categories. The final-verdict union fix and bidirectional duplicate-pair fix remain independently valid for non-colliding IDs.

Pass 4: Reviewed the remaining target file for additional CRITICAL/HIGH issues not already in the registry.  
Result: no new high-impact issue survived registry deduplication. Apparent candidates map to existing entries: priority scoring for rejected verdicts, ignored `rejected_findings`, hard-cap rendering behavior, unsafe rendering of non-string evidence/severity, and unused `_rebuild_section` parameter.

Pass 5: Second consecutive no-new-finding pass.  
Result: convergence reached for my review scope.

Definitive stance: my three independent findings are duplicates of existing canonical registry entries, so I merged them instead of re-filing. No new discovery finding is submitted.
